comment: Rhodes is a terrible professor. His lectures are confusing and your grade is based off of just four exams. If you haven't taken calc before, do yourself a favor and avoid his class at all costs.

Professor Rhodes may earn the honor of being the worst professor at the University of Richmond. He only grades us on 4 exams and makes each one varying in difficulty. When you ask him to clarify why you got certain grades, he gets very defensive and rarely offers any explanation. His lectures are long and confusing. I taught myself everything.

If you took calc in high school, AND REMEMBER IT, take his class. He assigns no homework and his lectures are super confusing so you definitely wont learn anything from him. With that said his exams (which your grade is entirely based on) are doable if you already KNOW calc. Also attendance isn't mandatory so its possible to only go on tests days.

Almost done with a semester of his Calc 1 class. I thought that having taken calc in high school would make this a breeze. His explanations somehow manages to confused me on this I already was good at. Basically learned calculus right before the exams by using the book. He doesn't assign homework either. Really nice person though
Worst teacher I've ever had

Stay away from his class.  He is terrible at helping his students understand the material.  He is extremely confusing.  His test questions do not match up with the questions that are in the textbooks.  Find a better class to improve your GPA rather than not learning and getting a bad grade.   He is a really nice guy though.

So far I'm only a few weeks into Rhodes' class, and it's terrible. Basically we have just been reviewing algebraic concepts that I understood perfectly fine in high school, yet somehow he has confused me to the point where simple problems appear incredibly complex. Probably better off not going to class and using Khan Academy to teach myself...

I would not suggest this professor to anyone. Thank god I took AP Calc because I didn't learn a single thing from this class. He explains simple concepts in the most confusing ways and his lectures are so boring. But in the end I got a decent grade for a class I put no effort into, so I really shouldn't have anything to complain about.

Extremely boring and long class. All he does is talk through his own steps in solving the problem. Is not good at clarifying. He is a smart guy, just not a good teacher. Does not assign homework, so you definitely slack off. If you haven't taken calculus previously, I would not recommend taking his class.

Class is extremely boing and can be difficult to follow. Doesn't use blackboard, inconvenient office hours. If you took calc in high school you might be ok, but if you haven't you will definitely struggle. Doesn't assign homework, which sounds nice but honestly makes you lazy and less likely to do work outside of class.

Burgess is an awful teacher. It is 12 weeks into the semester and he doesnt know anyone's names. Our class average for the first test was a 66%. He does not teach well. He knows what he is talking about but is very confusing. There is no work or homework, so you only have 3 tests which are NOT OPEN BOOK. Awful class, take someone else.

For Calculus I, Rhodes is likely the easiest teacher out there. He can also be very helpful if you review problems with him after class has ended. In class, he speaks rather confusingly to everyone who is a non-math major. The tests only check for a basic understanding of Calculus concepts, although the final is more challenging.

Extremely boring. Take him if you've taken calc before simply because he doesn't give homework. But there are 4 tests, so it's your responsibility to study hard for those days... But other than that it's a breeze.

His lectures are veryyy boring. You have to do a lot of work outside of class to understand the material. He is willing to answer questions but you have to independently do practice problems in order to have questions to ask. The class is hard if you've never had calculus but his tests are very fair.

No homework ever,3 exams worth 60% and a 40% final. For those who have taken calc and have done well this class is a breeze! Just read the textbook every now and then and you'll get an A. Don't take this class if you haven't taken calc before or are bad at it. You will probably fail. Take a teacher who gives hw and teaches better.

The most boring lectures of my life.  Nice guy, but does not relate to students. Never gives hw, never teaches things you'll see on tests. Attendance in optional, and if you go you are pretty much wasting time.  Teaches class as if they know the subject already.  READ the textbook before class or you'll be lost the entire time.
What a quirky guy! Makes tons of jokes that are just silly.  Tests are open book and open notes, but study the material before, so you don't spend the whole test looking stuff up.

He doesn't teach the material well and the only good grades in the class were received by those who had either already taken calc or spent alot of time teaching it to themselves. If you have taken calc before, take him and you will do well.

If you have taken calc before this will be an easy grade for you. Tests are not hard, however he is not very good at explaining things, so if you already have the knowledge or the ability to teach yourself you should get an easy a

open book open notes on his final.  grading system makes it possible to get a high letter grade with a low numerical average.  does not really teach concepts, expects you to come to class having read and practiced in the book.  spends class time going over problems and questions from the book, many that are more advanced than the material on tests

really nice guy-open notes, open book for the final. sometimes a little confusing for people with no calc background but is very willing to meet with students and is extremely helpful outside of class. the students who do poorly in his class lack self motivation. he doesn't assign homework so the class depends a lot on your own drive. rewards effor

No open book or notes, except for the final. He's a nice guy who tries his best. He can be flaky at times. And he's a visiting professor so finding a time to meet with him outside of class can be challenging. Material on the tests doesn't seem too hard.

I don't know where everyone is getting this open book idea, b/c in calculus it is closed book, no notes, NO CALCULATOR! Like others have said he is very out of touch with the students and boring. Unless you've already taken calculus in high school or can teach yourself I would not reccommend this class.

A little out of touch with students, but he tries to help everyone out. The entire class is curved, he gives extra credit, and allows you to use your textbook, old tests, and notes on the final. He is really helpful if you go and see him outside of class.

Professor Rhodes is a great professor. Most people taking this class don't want to take it, but it's not that bad. It is boring, but Rhodes is not a hard professor and will help you if you ask for it.

Rhodes is an easy teacher. His tests are open book and he didn't give homework. I never studied and barely paid attention in his class and passed with a B+. He gave three tests and the final, averages the grade for your final grade. He's a nice guy and I learned some interesting facts, totally unrelated to statistics.

Professor Rhodes is a nice guy, and he means well. His tests are open book because he said he realizes that in the real world you don't need to memorize facts. Most people take this class because it is required. He tries to make math interesting, but I don't really like math. Still a pretty good professor, though!
The test are very hard but his curve is very liberal... you don't have to do homework of you don't want to... tries to make the classes bearable but he is a bit out of touch with students

He is very boring, especially for a Tuesday/Thursday class at 8:15 am it can be hard to stay awake. He does mean well, his tests are open-book. Attendance is not mandatory, but its advised that you go because he does have an attendance sheet every class. The class itself is pretty easy if you understand the material - you can teach yourself.

Had him for social science stats. Found him unresponsive to students and very out of touch with what students want/need. Bonus: his tests are open book/note, but it might not be worth it because he is really boring (just repeats info from the book).
